solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Check carton isn't damaged

indicators.note: Something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged.

parts.note: The letters to rearrange.

explanation.surface: A shopper inspects a parcel and finds the box is intact.
explanation.walkthrough: "Check" reads as a verb in the surface, but it is the noun: a check is a restraint.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a restraint that holds something back, as in keeping costs in check.

clue.text: Finished on time, that's obvious

parts.note: When something is finished it is over.
T is the standard abbreviation for time.

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a job clearly came in on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: "On" just places T after OVER in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means done openly, plain to see: obvious.

clue.text: Little time for another helping

definitions.meaning: A small unit of time, several of them.
A further plateful taken at a meal, in British and US usage alike.

explanation.surface: A diner has only a moment left but wants more food.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses of SECONDS: tiny units of time, and a further plateful at a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking for seconds is asking for another helping of food.

clue.text: Fled wet weather, leaving island

indicators.note: The island's letter leaves the word, so it is removed.

parts.note: Wet weather is rain.
I is the standard abbreviation for island; take it out of RAIN.

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers escape the downpour by quitting an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the I from RAIN to leave RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ran, as in ran away, is the past tense of flee.

clue.text: Sienna set terribly unfeeling

indicators.note: Done terribly, the letters come out badly arranged.

parts.note: The letters to rearrange.

explanation.surface: A woman called Sienna is described as coldly indifferent.
explanation.walkthrough: Sienna looks like a name (or a colour), but it is only letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Insensate means lacking sensation or sympathy: unfeeling.

clue.text: Singer given £10 note, I hear

indicators.note: What I hear is a sound, so the answer sounds like the wordplay.

parts.note: A tenner is British slang for a ten-pound note.

explanation.surface: A performer is paid with a ten-pound note.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is everyday British slang for a £10 note; spoken, it matches TENOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male singer with a high voice.

clue.text: High as a kite, as Olive might be

definitions.meaning: Slang for heavily intoxicated on cannabis or other drugs.
An olive may have its pit taken out before serving.

explanation.surface: Someone called Olive is suspected of being very high.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital makes Olive look like a woman's name; it is the fruit, whose pit is called a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang sense: intoxicated on drugs; the other sense is an olive with its pit removed.

clue.text: Act as a prisoner's guiding light

parts.note: To act as something is to be it.
Used as written.
A con is a convict, a prisoner.

explanation.surface: Someone serves as the light that guides a prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: "Act as" looks like one phrase, but "as" is only surface glue and "Act" alone gives BE.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a light or fire used as a signal or guide.

clue.text: Boy at back tackling advanced piece of music

indicators.note: AT goes at the back of the boy.
Tackling means taking on, so A is added next.

parts.note: A boy is a son.
Used as written.
A is the standard abbreviation for advanced.

explanation.surface: A young footballer at the back makes a tackle and pushes forward.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture hides simple assembly: SON with AT behind it, then A.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonata is a composition for one or two instruments.

clue.text: Shock fans from the east

indicators.note: Read from the east, i.e. right to left in an across clue.

parts.note: Fans of something are nuts, enthusiasts.

explanation.surface: Supporters from the east are left shocked.
explanation.walkthrough: "Fans" means enthusiasts, as in football nuts, not cooling devices.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: to daze or astonish someone.

clue.text: Challenge Charlie about appearance

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet.
About, as in a talk on a subject, is ON.
A front is an outward show or appearance.

explanation.surface: Someone takes Charlie to task over how he looks.
explanation.walkthrough: "About" is not a container here; it simply gives ON, as in a book on birds.
explanation.definitionFit: To confront someone is to challenge them face to face.

clue.text: Lizard messing up clean home

indicators.note: Messing up puts the letters into disorder.

parts.note: The letters to rearrange.

explanation.surface: A pet lizard makes a mess of a tidy house.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads naturally as a lizard wrecking a house; the whole of "clean home" is the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a lizard famous for changing colour to match its surroundings.

clue.text: Not all change is hard for hostess

indicators.note: Only part of the following words is used.

parts.note: chanGE IS HArd.

explanation.surface: Adapting is difficult for the woman running a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the word breaks in "change is hard".
explanation.definitionFit: A geisha is a Japanese woman trained to entertain and host guests.

clue.text: Team still holding the French

indicators.note: One word holds the other inside it.

parts.note: Still, as in still better, can mean even.
LE is French for the.

explanation.surface: A squad keeps hold of some French players.
explanation.walkthrough: "Still" in the sense of "still more" means even, not motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket team has eleven players, so is called an eleven.

clue.text: Quarrelling when around Fleet Street barber?

indicators.note: One word goes around the other.

parts.note: When and as are interchangeable, as in as I arrived.
Sweeney Todd, the demon barber of Fleet Street.

explanation.surface: People fall out over a barber on Fleet Street.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street is a London street, home of the fictional murderous barber Sweeney Todd of the musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: people in disagreement are said to be at odds with each other.

clue.text: Old boy's remedy is little known

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil; add the S.
A remedy is a cure.

explanation.surface: A former pupil's treatment turns out to be little known.
explanation.walkthrough: An old boy is a former pupil of a British school, abbreviated OB; the possessive S is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: not widely known about, like an obscure poet.

clue.text: Seek Nero out for something to fan the flames?

indicators.note: Out, as in out of order, signals the letters are rearranged.

parts.note: The letters to rearrange.

explanation.surface: Hunting the emperor Nero, who fiddled while Rome burned, for fuel to spread the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: Nero is linked to the burning of Rome, so the fire picture fits; the question mark flags that the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerosene is paraffin, a fuel that feeds a fire.

clue.text: Booze supplier contributing to giftshop tickets

indicators.note: The answer contributes letters to the words that follow.

parts.note: giftshOP TICkets.

explanation.surface: A drinks firm sponsors tickets sold at a gift shop.
explanation.walkthrough: An optic is a British pub device fixed to an upside-down spirits bottle that dispenses a measured shot.
explanation.definitionFit: An optic supplies spirits in exact measures behind a bar.

clue.text: Betray group of agents to dictator

indicators.note: A dictator here is someone dictating, speaking words out loud, so we go by sound.

parts.note: A cell is a small group of spies or agents.

explanation.surface: A spy ring is handed over to a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: "Dictator" suggests a tyrant, but here it is someone who dictates, speaking words for another to write down.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to sell someone down the river is to betray them.

clue.text: Call up about one's flowering plant

indicators.note: In a down clue, up means read from bottom to top.
The word goes about, around, the other.

parts.note: Used as written.
One is I, the Roman numeral.

explanation.surface: Someone phones to talk about their lilac bush.
explanation.walkthrough: Put I inside CALL to make CALIL, then read it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a shrub with fragrant purple or white flowers.

clue.text: Decide on pay

definitions.meaning: To reach a decision about something, like a date.
To pay what is owed, as with a bill or account.

explanation.surface: Two parties agree what the wage will be.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as "decide on the pay"; split it after "on".
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to fix on a choice, and to clear a bill.

clue.text: Sally regularly holds cup in self-satisfied way

indicators.note: Take letters at regular intervals: S, L, Y.
The outer word holds the other inside it.

parts.note: The first, third and fifth letters of Sally.
A mug is a cup.

explanation.surface: A woman called Sally clutches her cup looking pleased with herself.
explanation.walkthrough: Sally looks like a woman's name but is only a source of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: in a complacent, pleased-with-oneself manner.

clue.text: So fed up, having lost £1000

indicators.note: The word has lost a letter, which is removed.

parts.note: Fed up, as in sick of it.
K stands for a thousand, as in £5k; remove it.

explanation.surface: Someone is so fed up after losing a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: "So" looks like an intensifier for "fed up"; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-only sense: the Latin word for thus, printed in quotations to mark an error as original.

clue.text: Voice telling you what's wrong with Conservative discipline

parts.note: CON is the standard abbreviation for Conservative.
A discipline is a field of study, such as a science.

explanation.surface: Someone's inner voice objects to Tory-style strictness.
explanation.walkthrough: Conservative refers to the British Tory party; "discipline" means a subject of study, not punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Your conscience is the inner voice that tells you right from wrong.
